name: ai_query_service.py
summary: Orchestrates the end-to-end AI query pipeline from natural language input to validated SQL execution and chart selection.
purpose: Acts as a unified facade that coordinates specialized AI sub-services to transform natural language questions into database queries and data visualizations, abstracting the complexity of prompt engineering, SQL generation, validation, execution, and chart recommendation behind a single service boundary.
responsibilities: Orchestrate the multi-stage AI query processing pipeline
Delegate prompt construction to PromptBuilder for SQL generation context
Coordinate SQL generation via SQLAgent using LLM capabilities
Enforce safety and correctness via SQLValidator before execution
Execute validated SQL via SQLExecutor and retrieve result sets
Determine optimal visualization via ChartSelector based on result schema
Capture execution timing and pipeline performance metrics
Propagate and handle failures between pipeline stages
outputs: Query result sets from executed SQL
Validation errors or pipeline stage failures
architecture_notes: Implements the Facade and Orchestrator patterns to unify a complex, multi-stage AI pipeline behind a single service interface. The class exhibits high cohesion as a pure coordination layer with no direct business logic, delegating to specialized collaborators (PromptBuilder, SQLAgent, SQLValidator, SQLExecutor, ChartSelector) to maintain separation of concerns and independent testability. The import of `time` suggests ad-hoc performance instrumentation, indicating this is a critical path service where latency matters. Located within a dedicated `ai` service package, it reinforces domain-driven design boundaries by isolating AI-specific orchestration from core business logic.
improvements: Replace ad-hoc `time` instrumentation with structured observability (distributed tracing and structured logging) across all pipeline stages
Introduce async/await patterns for non-blocking I/O during LLM calls and database execution
Add a circuit breaker and retry policy with exponential backoff for external AI service invocations to prevent cascade failures
Implement an intermediate caching layer for repeated natural language queries to reduce LLM token costs and latency
Refactor sequential stage calls into a formal Pipeline or Chain of Responsibility pattern to support configurable branching and conditional execution
Add explicit read-only SQL enforcement or query classification to mitigate security risks from LLM-generated SQL
Introduce input sanitization, rate limiting, and query cost estimation at the facade entry point
Decouple chart selection from query execution by emitting domain events, enabling asynchronous visualization rendering
